title: Leaves caught in the branches on the way down
question: Which one reads as leaves falling to the forest floor rather than collecting in the tree? (magenta = litter resting on a branch, cyan = litter resting on the ground)
context_md:
Your report: leaves fall off trees, get stuck and build up in the branches; they
should just fall through to the ground, because the world is a 2D slice of a 3D
one.

Both panes are `litter_probe`'s own overlay, same scene, same seed, 12,000
frames, one build each. The world is dimmed to a quarter so the two markers
read: **magenta = a litter cell resting on living tissue, cyan = a litter cell
resting on the ground.** Crop x110..400, y88..216, at 3x.

Discrete counts, same runs:

|  | left/right as stored A | as stored B |
|---|---|---|
| standing litter cells | 573 | 497 |
| ...resting on plant tissue | 330 (57.6%) | 219 (44.1%) |
| ...more than 32 rows above the ground | 23% | **0%** |
| ...more than 16 rows above the ground | 31% | 8% |
| still airborne at frame 12,000 | 4 | 0 |

And `crown_census frames=28800 trees=8`, the instrument the bug register's §V3
uses, same seed both arms — this is the "soil build-up in between the branches"
you named on card `20260824T014630073Z-a10698`:

| band | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| y120–160, litter | 283 | **25** |
| y120–160, soil | 84 | **6** |
| y80–120, litter + soil | 11 | **0** |
| highest row holding any soil | y 115 | **y 145** |
| total soil above the ground line | 508 | 498 |

The total soil is unchanged; it is no longer in the canopy.

What is left in magenta in the better arm is the drift banked up against a
trunk at floor level — a litter cell is a grid cell and cannot sit *behind* a
tree the way the gnome can, so a pile resting on a root collar scores as
"resting on plant". That is `litter.ron`'s 42-degree friction angle working.
